clue.text: They don't like to strike

parts.note: reads like workers reluctant to down tools, but means people opposed to hitting anyone or waging war

explanation.surface: A grumble about workers who won't join industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests a walkout by a union; the real sense is to hit or attack, which these people refuse to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacifists oppose violence and war, so they refuse to strike a blow.

clue.text: Influence of converted priest, say, is mounting

indicators.note: converted means the letters of priest are changed into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means the piece climbs upwards, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A clergyman who has changed faith is gaining standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges PRIEST into PRESTI; 'is mounting' turns EG upwards to GE in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is standing or reputation that gives a person sway over others.

clue.text: The nerve of the chap

definitions.meaning: nerve in the sense of impudence or effrontery
a chap (as in chaps or chops) is the jaw or side of the face

explanation.walkthrough: 'chap' looks like a man, but here it is the old word for the jaw or side of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudence is called cheek, and the fleshy side of the face is also a cheek, as is a chap.

clue.text: KLM pilot not allowed to make a landing?

definitions.text: KLM pilot not allowed to make a landing?

parts.words: KLM pilot not allowed to make a landing?
parts.note: KLM is the Dutch airline, so its pilot is an airborne Dutchman; the legendary ghost ship's captain was doomed never to make landfall

explanation.surface: An airline captain from the Netherlands is refused permission to touch down.
explanation.walkthrough: The legend tells of a phantom ship condemned to sail forever, never reaching port; 'landing' covers both aircraft and ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary phantom ship and its captain are condemned never to reach harbour, as the clue's grounded airman suggests.

clue.text: A little bit of heaven?

parts.note: a fraction of a whole is a little bit, and the phrase about supreme bliss pairs this ordinal with heaven

explanation.surface: A wistful description of a blissful moment.
explanation.walkthrough: One part in seven is a small portion, and the idiom for supreme happiness is to be in the heaven of that number.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-in-seven fraction is a small share, and the idiom for bliss joins this word to heaven.

clue.text: Unintellectual impression about sunburst

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a seal is an impression stamped in wax

indicators.note: burst means the letters of sun are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A physical sensation felt when the sun breaks through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sunburst' reads as one word, a burst of sunshine, but it splits: 'burst' is the anagram signal working on the first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sensual appeals to the bodily senses rather than to the mind, so it is unintellectual.

clue.text: Aged? By Jove, it might be!

indicators.note: it might be suggests that the word aged could become this exclamation once its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at being asked if they are old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aged' rearranged gives the old oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated mild oaths expressing surprise, interchangeable in old-fashioned speech.

clue.text: In Italian it translates as "sliding one's fingers along the keyboards"

definitions.text: In Italian it translates as "sliding one's fingers along the keyboards"

parts.words: In Italian it translates as "sliding one's fingers along the keyboards"
parts.note: describes the musical term, Italianate in form, for a rapid slide over the keys

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry for an Italian musical term.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is a pseudo-Italian plural formed from French glisser, to slide, which is why the clue reads like a translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Glissandi are rapid slides through a run of notes, made on a piano by sweeping a finger along the keys.

clue.text: Assimilate a summary

definitions.meaning: a condensed version of a longer text

explanation.definitionFit: To digest is to absorb food or information, and a digest is also a condensed summary.

clue.text: Drying up, I'd lark about with writer

indicators.note: about means the letters of the preceding words are moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A washer-up fools around with an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the fourteen letters of DRYING UP and I'D LARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling was the English author of The Jungle Book and Kim.

clue.text: Each cigarette end needs a light

indicators.note: the last letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the end of the word cigarette is the letter E
a Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol

explanation.surface: Every smoker wants someone to light their cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link. A Very light is a flare named after its inventor, not a match or lighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Each and every are synonyms meaning all members of a group taken individually.

clue.text: Risking a commercial undertaking, given turn around

indicators.note: around means the letters of given and turn are spun round into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Taking a business gamble when the market changes direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs to five words; 'Risking' alone would leave 'a commercial undertaking' with no job, and a venture is exactly such an undertaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A venture is a risky business enterprise, so venturing is risking money on a commercial undertaking.

clue.text: Admitted being deceived?

definitions.meaning: let in, as a guest or new member

explanation.surface: A question whether someone allowed entry has been fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning both welcomed inside and fooled or conned by a trick.

clue.text: Sly Sue's destroyed Joyce's character

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of the previous words are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
the possessive s is used here as a letter

explanation.surface: A cunning woman has wrecked a famous novelist's character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges SLYSUES.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce's novel takes its title from the Latin name of Homer's hero Odysseus, whose wanderings shape Leopold Bloom's day.

clue.text: Issues involving one's offspring

parts.note: issue means descendants, so this is the issue that comes from one's own children

explanation.surface: Problems concerning one's children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issues' looks like problems, but it means descendants: the children of one's children.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandparent's descendants through their own sons and daughters form the second generation of their issue.

clue.text: Irresolute chairman's lack of control

indicators.note: irresolute means wavering, so the letters of chairman's are unsettled and reordered

parts.note: the possessive s is used here as a letter

explanation.surface: An indecisive chairman fails to keep order in the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irresolute' rearranges CHAIRMANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism is the doctrine of no government, a state without rule or control.

clue.text: Vandalised rose beds need patient care

definitions.note: the definition reads as things that need patient care, plural like the answer

indicators.note: vandalised means the letters of rose and beds are smashed up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener's flowerbeds have been trampled and must be nursed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vandalised' rearranges ROSEBEDS. 'patient care' looks like a gardener's patience; it is nursing for a hospital patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure ulcers form on bedridden people and require careful nursing.

clue.text: Back in time

parts.note: reads like time travel, but means moving the way a clock's hands would go in reverse

explanation.surface: A phrase about travelling into the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in time' suggests the past; it describes direction measured against a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning against the direction of a clock's hands is moving backwards relative to the timepiece.

clue.text: Two pounds in hard cash for "The Moonstone" author

indicators.note: in means the pounds are placed inside the cash

parts.note: coins are hard money as opposed to notes
L is the abbreviation for a pound, so two pounds give two Ls

explanation.surface: A couple of quid paid in coin for a Victorian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: L for pound comes from Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilkie Collins wrote The Moonstone, an early English detective novel.

clue.text: Scrap an out-of-date golf club

parts.note: something out of date is old
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Throw away an obsolete golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for scrap metal; 'an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap metal is commonly called this, as in a rag-and-bone man's cry.

clue.text: Insect with the ability to irritate?

parts.note: may expresses being able or permitted
to bug someone is to annoy them

explanation.surface: A question whether an insect has the power to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The maybug, or cockchafer, is a large beetle that appears in spring.

clue.text: Where is this sold? Oh, in the local, perhaps

definitions.text: Where is this sold? Oh, in the local, perhaps

indicators.note: in means the exclamation is placed inside the rearranged word
perhaps suggests the letters of local are only possibly in this order and may be changed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks where drink can be bought and is told the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the local is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub, where drink is sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Drink containing ethanol is sold in pubs, the local being the neighbourhood pub.

clue.text: Lower speeds ordered on both sides of the river

indicators.note: on both sides of means the rearranged letters flank the river abbreviation
ordered means the letters of speeds are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Boats slow down on either bank of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges SPEEDS into DEPESS, split around R.
explanation.definitionFit: To depress something is to push it down, the verb sense of lower.

clue.text: Run over?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a run scored from a wide or bye rather than the bat

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a run conceded by the bowling side through a wide, no-ball or bye is not credited to the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a run not off the bat is given this name, and anything surplus is left over.

clue.text: Officer getting a rough ride on ship

indicators.note: on means the following pieces are placed after the ship

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship

indicators.note: rough means the letters of ride are roughed up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A military man has a bumpy voyage at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link; 'rough' rearranges RIDE into DIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army officer commanding a brigade.

clue.text: Bury in Milan?

parts.note: Bury is an English football club, and the Milan counterpart is a famous club whose name is also a verb meaning bury

explanation.surface: A question about a burial taking place in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town and football club in Lancashire; Milan's club is Internazionale, known by this short name, which also means to bury.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body, and the Milan football club is called by this name.

clue.text: Lame ducks, maybe

definitions.meaning: ... describes a crippled or injured leg
ducks are an example of birds hunted for sport and food

explanation.definitionFit: A game leg is a lame one, and wild birds shot for sport such as ducks are called game.

clue.text: It suffers periodic reversals in time

definitions.text: It suffers periodic reversals in time

parts.words: It suffers periodic reversals in time
parts.note: describes a timer that must be turned upside down at intervals to keep measuring

explanation.surface: A remark about something whose fortunes keep turning over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversals' sounds like setbacks; it is literal turning over of the device.
explanation.definitionFit: An hourglass with sand must be inverted each time the sand runs through, to keep timing.
